title: Does the Opus writer advantage generalise? Opus xhigh against Sonnet high (twice) on six new key-step pages and three controls

document.name: nlogn
document.title: Integer multiplication below n log n (paper.tex)

task: exposition: write tasks for six key-step pages (0018, 0021, 0031, 0032, 0033, 0036) and three controls (0005, 0006, 0010), from E9F4Y's fixed plan; 24 page-runs judged by three blind Opus judges each (J26)
question: Is Opus xhigh better than Sonnet high on key-step pages in general (k of 6), and does Sonnet high meet the fidelity standard there (rule R2)?

binary.commit: exegenius 0.6.0 (target/debug/exegenius sha256 c37a2b3d…caee8), not rebuilt during the run

protocol: general-purpose subagents launched from the development session, up to 20 at a time; judges by pointer prompt to J24's judge text (calibration/plans/W3.md)
preregistration: calibration/plans/W3.md (preregistered 05:31 UTC, 2026-10-15; amendment 2 at 06:49 UTC, 2026-10-17; launch readiness 08:42; all before any run)
comparison: W2b's per-page rule (WO against WS) on key-step pages; errors only on controls; rule R2 over 12 Sonnet and 6 Opus page-runs

intended.task_prompt: the write task as rendered by exegenius 0.6.0 in a copy of E9F4Y's project
as WS (a second run, key-step pages only)

primary_preregistered.value: k = 2 (Opus better on 0018 and 0036; Sonnet on 0032; 3 tied); controls Opus 2 of 3. Row 3: page-specific, no rollout

R2.value: 8 of 12 Sonnet page-runs fail the standard (0018, 0031, 0032, 0036, both runs); Opus fails on 0031 and 0032, so R2 is inconclusive

decision.value: status quo: Sonnet high writes, Opus xhigh on 0015/0016 in this wiki; no default change

exploratory.value: faithful equals derived in every cell but one count: the gap is derivation, not error (1 major error in 24 page-runs, 0018 WS). On 0036 Sonnet derives medians 4 and 3 of 19 steps, Opus 18. Two cells have one outlying judge (0032 WO; 0036 WS2)

cache_read_tokens.value: runs 38.4 M (WO 19.2, WS 11.3, WS2 7.9); J26 33.0 M for 72 judgements

deviations.what: J26 judges received a pointer prompt to J24's judge text (paths changed) rather than the pasted text
stage 2 (J26) ran on the author's standing instruction and the five-hour limit's status 'allowed', not on a fresh meter reading

limitations: Six key-step pages and three controls of one paper; one Opus run and two Sonnet runs per key-step page.
The fidelity standard is strict at 18 steps (17 needed); judge disagreement is large on two cells.
